ns2:section.sectionText: WILDLIFE CONSERVATION AND COMMUNITIES BOTSWANA The course provides students with a hands-on research experience through a 2-week winter excursion on wildlife conservation and communities in Botswana. Students will attend a 5-day lecture series at the research camp, with field excursions, to prepare them for being part of a research team and to understand the dynamic coexistence of humans and wildlife. Then, students will join the research team for 5 days to learn field techniques, collect data and understand the reality and vision behind field research. The student?s time in the field will focus on the two main objectives of Wildlife ACT: (1) implementing a standardized biodiversity monitoring protocol for Botswana?s Department of Wildlife & National Parks, and (2) conducting human-wildlife conflict studies and implementing mitigation strategies with the University of Botswana?s Okavango Research Institute (ORI). Students will learn how to set up a field research project, from project design to data collection and implementation, and will gain valuable skills and knowledge. STUDY ABROAD FEES APPLY.
